heroHeadline: DeepSeek Declares AGI Mission as State-Led $10B Round Closes at ~$50B — China's Most Disruptive AI Lab Formally Backed by National Capital at APEC AI Forum in Suzhou
heroSubtitle: May 22, 2026 — DeepSeek founder and CEO Liang Wenfeng declared artificial general intelligence (AGI) as the company's primary long-term mission on May 22 as its first external funding round advanced toward close at approximately $50 billion valuation — the highest valuation of any Chinese AI startup. The 70 billion yuan (~$10B) round is led by China's national Big Fund III (CICIIF), with Tencent participating, and represents the formal entry of state capital into DeepSeek's equity structure. Liang told investors the company will prioritize groundbreaking research over commercialization while maintaining its open-source commitment. The AGI declaration is the first from a major Chinese AI lab, placing DeepSeek in direct frontier competition with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind — not merely on benchmark metrics but on the full AGI mission. The primary funding driver is talent retention: DeepSeek's researchers are being aggressively recruited by better-capitalized rivals. Simultaneously, APEC 2026 Trade Ministers convened in Suzhou under China's chairmanship — the first major multilateral AI governance forum of the year — where the US announced it is 'very active in promoting U.S. AI options and solutions' across Asia-Pacific, and China's Commerce Minister Li Chenggang promoted Beijing's 'open cooperation' AI governance vision to regional partners. These two events represent the twin escalation axes of the US-China tech competition: domestic AI frontier investment (DeepSeek AGI + Big Fund) and international norm-setting competition (APEC AI governance battle in Suzhou). They follow a week of structural milestones: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly conceded China's AI chip market to Huawei on May 21; Alibaba unveiled the Zhenwu M890 claiming 3x Nvidia H20 performance on May 20; and China's 15th Five-Year Plan AI+ action plan is mandating 70% domestic silicon wafer use and 50% domestic chipmaking equipment for new fabs — creating a domestic AI tech stack that is increasingly self-contained from US technology access.
